rule: Likelihood and impact are qualitative (low / medium / high) and are the analyst's judgement on a verified factual base. Where an official probability exists it is quoted in `official_basis`. No quantitative probability is invented.

classes.BAU: Business as usual - the ordinary operating, market, credit and fiscal risks that should be priced in every year.
classes.SWAN: Rare, high-severity event that could impair the local economy or the asset itself. Not priced by the market most days.

rows.risk: Tenant same-store sales keep falling and the franchisee at this location becomes unable to pay contract rent.
rows.mechanism: System same-store sales were -1.1% in Q3 FY2026 and franchise-level margin fell from 39.3% to 37.4%. A single-restaurant franchisee absorbs closures and weak volume before the parent does.
rows.mitigation: Read the franchisee's financial statements before any renewal decision; require a corporate or personal guaranty at renewal; consider a security deposit; verify rent coverage from the franchisee's P&L, not from the parent's disclosure.
rows.official_basis: Same-store sales (1.1%) decline, franchise-level margin 37.4%, bad-debt expense higher year over year (S15).

rows.risk: The brand closes this restaurant as part of a rationalisation programme while the lease is still running.
rows.mechanism: Restaurant count fell from 2,168 to 2,115 in twelve months, with 17 closures in Q3 alone, attributed in the release to the 'JACK on Track' closure programme.
rows.mitigation: Obtain the franchise agreement term and the parent's development/closure criteria; negotiate a closure-notice covenant and a termination fee at renewal; keep the land value case underwritten so the site survives vacancy.
rows.official_basis: 2,115 restaurants at 2026-07-05 vs 2,168 a year earlier; 17 closures in the quarter (S15).

rows.risk: The lease is with a franchisee, not with Jack in the Box Inc., so the parent's balance sheet provides no credit support.
rows.mechanism: Jack in the Box is overwhelmingly franchised (1,966 of 2,115 units). The parent's cash of $46.3m and $1.43bn of debt do not automatically stand behind a franchisee's rent.
rows.mitigation: Identify the named tenant and read the guaranty. If there is no parent guaranty, the asset is franchisee-credit, and both the sale price and the hold case must reflect that.
rows.official_basis: Franchised 1,966 of 2,115 units; cash $46,318k; long-term debt $1,428,667k (S15, S16).

rows.risk: The county's trade-area population keeps shrinking, so restaurant volume and therefore rent coverage erode.
rows.mechanism: County population is -3.2% since the 2020 Census base and the state projects a further 215,911 person decline to 2040. Fewer households is fewer transactions for a limited-service restaurant.
rows.mitigation: Price the asset on the land and on the site's own traffic, not on county growth. Any renewal should be at or above current rent, never at a discount for 'market' reasons unless a rental survey proves the discount.
rows.official_basis: County population 9,694,934 (-3.2% since 2020) (S02); official projections 9,853,435 (2025) to 9,637,524 (2040) (S03).

rows.risk: Statutory wage floors rise faster than the tenant can reprice, squeezing restaurant margin and rent-paying capacity.
rows.mechanism: Three overlapping floors now apply: state $16.90 (2026), fast food $20.00 (AB 1228), and City of Los Angeles $18.42 effective 2026-07-01. The ECI for the LA CSA is running +3.9% against +3.1% nationally.
rows.mitigation: Treat escalations as protection, not as a negotiating gift. A renewal with flat rent in a 3.9% wage-cost environment is a real rent cut.
rows.official_basis: State $16.90 effective 2026-01-01 (S07); fast food $20.00 (S08); City of LA $18.42 effective 2026-07-01 (S09); ECI LA CSA +3.9% (S05).

rows.risk: Household budgets in the trade area are too thin to support the tenant's pricing.
rows.mechanism: City median household income is $81,939 and the city poverty rate is 16.5%; both are worse than the county. Limited-service restaurants are the most exposed segment when real incomes compress.
rows.mitigation: Underwrite to the city, not the county, and prefer a renewal with a longer term and a stronger guaranty over a higher rent at a weaker credit.
rows.official_basis: City median household income $81,939; city poverty 16.5%; county $90,112 and 13.3% (S02).

rows.risk: Cap rates expand and the asset is worth less at expiry than it is today, so waiting to sell destroys value.
rows.mechanism: The 10-year Treasury is 4.88% and the current net-lease acquisition benchmark is a 6.8% initial cash yield. If either rises, a buyer's required yield rises with it and the price falls.
rows.mitigation: The model solves for the exit cap at which holding and selling tie, and publishes it, so the decision can be made against an observable number rather than a forecast.
rows.official_basis: 10-year Treasury 4.88% on 2026-11-09 (S01); net-lease initial weighted average cash yield 6.8% in Q3 2026 (S17).

rows.risk: Sale proceeds cannot be redeployed at a yield high enough to beat holding.
rows.mechanism: Selling only wins if the after-cost proceeds earn more than the asset does. That required yield is a solved number in the model, and it is sensitive to the reinvestment assumption.
rows.mitigation: Do not list without an identified replacement pipeline. A 1031 exchange requires like-kind US real property (S14); cash in a taxable account at 4.38%-4.88% is not a substitute for a 6.8% net-lease yield.
rows.official_basis: Section 1031 relief applies to real property exchanges (S14); T-bill 4.38% and 10-year 4.88% (S01); net-lease benchmark 6.8% (S17).

rows.risk: The cost of selling is higher than assumed because the price crosses a Measure ULA threshold.
rows.mechanism: City transfer tax is 0.45% below $5.4m but 4.45% between $5.4m and $10.9m and 5.95% at or above $10.9m. A sale at $5.4m costs about $240k more than a sale at $5.39m.
rows.mitigation: Model the after-tax price at the actual negotiated number, not an average rate. If the value lands just above a threshold, the marginal cost of the last dollar is punitive and the negotiation should reflect it.
rows.official_basis: Base 0.45%; ULA 4% above $5,400,000 and 5.5% at $10,900,000 or more, effective for closings after 2026-06-30 (S10).

rows.risk: Property taxes jump after a sale because the Proposition 13 cap resets to the purchase price.
rows.mechanism: The 2% annual cap applies to the base-year value while the owner holds. A sale establishes a new base year, so the buyer prices the higher tax bill into the offer, and the seller's own replacement property carries the same reset.
rows.mitigation: Quantify the owner's effective tax rate as a percentage of value and compare it with the market rate. A long-held asset carries an implicit, transferable-to-nobody subsidy that disappears on sale - this is a genuine reason to hold, and it is a reason a buyer will discount.
rows.official_basis: Annual inflation factor may not exceed 2 percent of the prior year's value (RTC 51(a)(1)(D), S12).

rows.risk: One tenant, one parcel, one metro. A single adverse event removes a large share of the owner's net worth.
rows.mechanism: The asset is a single-tenant building in a single county. Its cash flow and its resale value are driven by the same two variables, tenant performance and local demand.
rows.mitigation: This is the strongest argument for exchanging rather than holding, and it is independent of cap rates. The Monte Carlo publishes the tail-loss difference between the concentrated and diversified paths rather than a mean difference.
rows.official_basis: The reference net-lease portfolio holds 15,536 properties leased to 1,842 clients (S17) - the diversification the subject owner does not have.

rows.risk: The owner starts the process too late and loses the option to choose.
rows.mechanism: A net-lease sale plus a 1031 identification takes months; the lease's option-notice date can fall earlier than the expiry. Running out of time converts a choice into a forced outcome.
rows.mitigation: Read the option notice clause first. Set a hard decision date at least 12 months before the earliest notice date, not before the expiry date.
rows.official_basis: Section 1031 requires the exchange to be structured as an exchange of real property (S14). The lease's own dates are unverified (L01, L04).

rows.risk: The owner decides on numbers that were assumed rather than read.
rows.mechanism: Rent, expiry, escalations, basis and debt are all unverified in this workbook. Every model output is an assumption set, and a precise-looking figure built on assumed rent is not evidence.
rows.mitigation: The model is published per $100,000 of rent and as a breakeven, not as an appraisal. Fill the 14 blanks on flag.html before committing capital.
rows.official_basis: 48 rows are blank in metrics.json, including the 14 lease and property fields L01-L14, the 4 tax fields X10-X13, the 2 tenant fields T13-T14 and the 6 owner-profile fields O01-O06.

rows.risk: A damaging earthquake destroys or closes the building, and the loss exceeds insurance recovery.
rows.mechanism: USGS puts the Los Angeles region at a 60% chance of M6.7+ in 30 years, 46% at M7.0+ and 31% at M7.5+. A drive-through is a lightweight structure, but the land, utilities and customer base are exposed, and business interruption is not covered by a standard property policy.
rows.mitigation: Obtain a parcel-level CGS seismic/liquefaction screening and a current earthquake quote; if uninsured or underinsured, this single exposure can exceed several years of rent. Diversification removes it; nothing else does.
rows.official_basis: Los Angeles region, 30-year likelihood: M>=6.7 60%, M>=7.0 46%, M>=7.5 31% (USGS UCERF3, S18).

rows.risk: A wildfire reaches the urban asset, or smoke and power shut-offs close it for weeks.
rows.mechanism: The Eaton Fire burned 14,021 acres inside Los Angeles County in January 2025, destroyed 9,419 structures and damaged 1,076. It started on 2025-01-07 and took 24 days to contain. A January fire in an urban-interface county is the relevant precedent, not a mountain-forest scenario.
rows.mitigation: Look up the parcel's Fire Hazard Severity Zone (CAL FIRE) and confirm the policy does not exclude fire following earthquake; check whether the carrier has withdrawn from the ZIP code. Insurance availability, not the fire itself, is often what destroys value.
rows.official_basis: Eaton Fire: 14,021 acres, 9,419 structures destroyed, 1,076 damaged, 19 fatalities, cause Electrical (CAL FIRE, S20); FHSZ framework and LRA maps (S19).

rows.risk: The property becomes uninsurable or insurable only at a cost that eliminates net income.
rows.mechanism: After a major loss event, carriers reprice or withdraw. The USGS fact sheet records that quake-risk repricing after Northridge produced an insurance-availability crisis resolved only by creating the California Earthquake Authority.
rows.mitigation: Obtain a quote now, in writing, with the renewal premium and the deductible. A buyer will do exactly this during diligence, so the owner should know the answer before listing.
rows.official_basis: The 1994 Northridge earthquake contributed to a homeowner-insurance-availability crisis resolved in 1996 by creating the California Earthquake Authority (S18). Current premium is unverified (H11).

rows.risk: The tenant or its franchisee enters bankruptcy and rejects the lease.
rows.mechanism: The parent carries negative stockholders' equity of -$901m and $1.43bn of long-term debt against $46m of cash, while same-store sales are negative. A franchisee is weaker than the parent.
rows.mitigation: A rejection in bankruptcy leaves the landlord with a vacancy and an unsecured claim. Prefer a parent guaranty at renewal, and keep a re-tenanting plan and a land-value floor in the underwriting.
rows.official_basis: Cash $46,318k; long-term debt $1,428,667k; total stockholders' deficit $(901,286)k at 2026-07-05 (S16).

rows.risk: Local or state tax and labour policy shifts raise the cost of owning or operating the asset.
rows.mechanism: Measure ULA already taxes City sales at 4.45% or 5.95% above indexed thresholds, and the thresholds rise annually with Chained CPI. Separately, three wage floors stack on the tenant. Both were live in 2026 and both can move again.
rows.mitigation: Recheck the ULA thresholds on the Office of Finance page before setting an asking price - they are CPI-indexed, so a stale number understates the tax.
rows.official_basis: ULA thresholds are adjusted annually on the BLS Chained CPI (S10); statutory wage floors (S07, S08, S09).

rows.risk: Long rates rise sharply and both the asset price and the refinancing capacity fall at once.
rows.mechanism: The 10-year is already 4.88% and the 30-year 5.26%, with a flat-to-inverted short end. A further move up compresses net-lease pricing, which is priced off spread to Treasuries.
rows.mitigation: The exit-cap sensitivity grid shows the break-even cap rate. If the owner intends to hold, the protection is rent escalation and a long remaining term, not a rate forecast.

rows.risk: A public-health or mobility shock closes dine-in and drive-through traffic for an extended period.
rows.mechanism: The information sector has lost 10,200 jobs in twelve months and motion-picture employment is contracting; a shock that reduces commuting reduces the drive-through's pass-by trade.
rows.mitigation: Business-interruption cover and a rent-abatement clause cap, negotiated at renewal. The asset cannot be made immune; the portfolio can.
rows.official_basis: Information sector -10,200 jobs year over year; declines in 20 of the last 22 months (S06).

rows.risk: An unknown easement, entitlement defect or environmental condition is discovered in a buyer's diligence and reprices or kills the sale.
rows.mechanism: Drive-through sites commonly carry reciprocal easement agreements, signage easements, or a legacy underground-storage issue. None of these appear in any official dataset; they appear in a title report and a Phase I.
rows.mitigation: Order title and a Phase I before listing, not after going under contract. A defect found by the buyer costs more than one found by the owner.
rows.official_basis: No official dataset covers this; recorded as an owner document request (L09, L10, L11).

rows.risk: The owner acts on this workbook as if it were an appraisal.
rows.mechanism: Every dollar figure here rests on a rent that was never supplied, a cap rate that no official source publishes, and a cost structure that was assumed. Precision in the output is not evidence in the input.
rows.mitigation: Use the breakevens and the triggers, not the dollar totals. Obtain a broker opinion of value and an appraisal before any transaction.
rows.official_basis: No official source publishes a single-asset cap rate (M11); fourteen owner fields are blank.
